:::{#exr-rank-transpose-practice}
#### Finding the rank of a Gram matrix without computing it

A [Gram matrix](#def-gram-matrix) can be larger than the [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) it comes from,
but @thm-rank-transpose says it has the same [rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-rank).
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \sbmat{1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1}.
$$

Find $\rankf{\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}}$ without computing $\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Find $\rankf{\matr{A}}$ from its two [rows](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-row), using @thm-rank-transpose once more.

:::
